title: [YouPass Collect] - European Medical Care Trends 1980-2000
prompt: The table shows information about medical care in three different European countries between 1980 and 2000. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features and make comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The table illustrates the number of physicians and hospital beds per 1000 people, as well as the average length of hospital stays, in Austria, France, and Sweden over three years: 1980, 1990, and 2000.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, while hospital beds increased across all three countries during this period, the figures for physicians and average hospital stays showed more varied trends. In addition, Sweden consistently led in most healthcare metrics throughout.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Regarding healthcare resources, Sweden had the highest number of physicians in 1980 at 3.6 per 1000 people, followed by France at 2.4, while Austria recorded the lowest figure of 0.8. Over the next two decades, Sweden's figure fluctuated, dropping to 3.0 in 1990 before rising to 3.8 by 2000. Meanwhile, France declined to 1.3, and Austria increased modestly to 1.0. As for hospital beds, Sweden again topped the list with 6.4 beds per 1000 people in 1980, compared to 1.4 in Austria and 0.2 in France. By 2000, all three nations witnessed growth, with France dramatically rising to 1.6, Austria to 3.7, and Sweden to 6.9.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: Turning to the average length of hospital stays, Sweden recorded the longest duration at 23 days in 1980, significantly higher than Austria's 18 days and France's 9 days. France demonstrated a consistent downward trend, with the figure falling to 7 days in 1990 and 5 days in 2000, while both Austria and Sweden experienced fluctuations, ending at 18 and 21 days respectively.
